title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 749 customers reveals an overall churn rate of 37.7%. Monthly-contract customers churn at more than double the rate of annual-contract customers. A high-risk segment of 100 customers (high support tickets, low satisfaction) churns at 71%. Premium-plan customers deliver nearly 4× the lifetime value of Basic customers, underscoring the revenue importance of retention at the top tier.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers with an overall churn rate of 37.7% and an average monthly fee of $42.11.
Churn rates differ modestly across plans: Basic is highest at 38.9%, followed by Standard at 36.7%, and Premium at 36.6%. The spread between Basic and Premium is approximately 2.3 percentage points.
Cohort churn rates are broadly stable across signup years but the 2024 cohort is highest at 39.8%, followed by 2021 at 38.0%, 2023 at 37.1%, and 2022 at 36.7%. No sustained downward trend is evident.

Contract type is a strong churn driver. Monthly-contract customers churn at 48.3% versus 21.9% for Annual customers — Monthly churn is 121% higher than Annual, indicating that longer commitments substantially reduce attrition.
100 customers meet the at-risk criteria (≥5 support tickets and satisfaction score ≤2). This segment churns at 71.0%, nearly double the overall rate, making it the highest-priority retention target.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months (median 19.0, SD 13.2), indicating a wide spread. Mean satisfaction is 3.4 out of 5, with 27 customers missing a satisfaction score.

Mean lifetime value rises sharply by plan: Basic $463, Standard $869, Premium $1,817. Premium LTV is 292% higher than Basic, confirming that retaining Premium customers is disproportionately valuable.

limitations: The 2024 cohort may be incomplete (customers signed up later in the year have had less time to churn), which could inflate or deflate its observed churn rate.
27 customers (3.6%) are missing satisfaction scores; their exclusion from satisfaction-based analyses may introduce a small bias if missingness is non-random.
Lifetime value is computed from available data fields and may not capture all revenue streams (e.g., add-ons, discounts), so absolute LTV figures should be treated as indicative.
The at-risk segment filter uses fixed thresholds (tickets ≥5, satisfaction ≤2); alternative thresholds could change segment size and churn rate.
The dataset is a single snapshot; causal relationships (e.g., whether low satisfaction causes churn) cannot be established from cross-sectional data alone.
conclusion: Churn is elevated across all segments at ~37.7%, but contract type and customer health signals are the clearest levers. Migrating monthly customers to annual contracts and intervening early with the 100 at-risk customers (71% churn rate) represent the highest-impact near-term actions. Given Premium customers generate 292% more lifetime value than Basic, targeted retention investment at the Premium tier offers the greatest financial return.
